The unconditional comparison is now explicitly between the full intrinsic measure and its restriction to positive original fibers. Equality is equivalent to zero contributions from the omitted bases because all components are nonnegative and their base labels are disjoint.

For every retained positive fiber, the restored null boundary-section condition makes slice indicators converge pointwise off a null set on parallel planes. Dominated convergence and Fubini give a two-sided first derivative equal to minus the restricted slice integral for a threshold increase.

The supporting-rectangle witness from the first review violates the restored condition, and the disk–segment witness satisfies the condition on the disk while the null fiber contributes to the full intrinsic section. Its asserted depth and centroid discrepancy persist.
Original and revision candidate IDs, source locators and dependency lists match, and the revision is linked to the exact initial reviewed bytes.
The rotation and shear fix the integer base and are isometries on each section fiber. They preserve the summed intrinsic measure with no ambient-plane Jacobian.
Proper crossing in the own fiber produces ambient interior points on both sides by mixing with an ambient interior point, proving the full section dimension.
The disk–segment example has actual raw depth pi over two and equal length sections at bases zero and one. The derivative measure lives only on the disk.
Source 867dbbe22c30cda2 §2(2) excludes positive section measure on supporting traces. Section 3a uses the derivative measure of §3 under that assumption. The frozen comparison does not retain it.
